record.paper_title: Report from the Open Problems Session at OPSFA13
record.original_question: What is the finite-dimensional spectrum of a random symmetric Bernoulli matrix, that is, a symmetric matrix whose entries are independently chosen as ±1 subject to symmetry, beyond the asymptotic universality statements known for Wigner ensembles?

evidence.quote: What is the spectrum of a ﬁnite-dimensional random symmetric Bernoulli matrix? A random symmetric Bernoulli matrix consists of entries that are randomly ±1, subject to a symmetry condition. What is the spectrum of a ﬁnite-dimensional random symmetric Bernoulli matrix? Unlike other symmetric random matrices such as Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE), these only have a ﬁnite number of conﬁgurations of eigenvalues. While such matrices fall into the general framework of universality for Wigner ensembles [19, 38] (describing the asymptotics of the spectrum), this does not explain the ﬁnite-dimensional picture.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer $n\ge 1$, let $M_n$ be a random $n\times n$ symmetric matrix whose entries on and above the diagonal are independent random variables, each taking the values $+1$ and $-1$ with probability $1/2$, and whose entries below the diagonal are determined by the symmetry condition $M_n(i,j)=M_n(j,i)$. Such a matrix is called a random symmetric Bernoulli matrix. Because the sample space is finite, $M_n$ takes only finitely many values and its spectrum has only finitely many possible configurations.

While Wigner-type universality describes the asymptotic spectral statistics of $M_n$ as $n\to\infty$ (semicircle law for the empirical spectral distribution, sine-kernel local statistics in the bulk, Tracy–Widom law at the edge), these asymptotic results do not describe the spectrum of $M_n$ for fixed finite $n$.

Problem: Give an explicit description of the joint distribution of the eigenvalues $\lambda_1(M_n)\le\cdots\le\lambda_n(M_n)$ of $M_n$ at finite $n$. In particular, determine, beyond the asymptotic universality statements, exact (non-asymptotic) formulas or characterizations for the finite-dimensional spectrum of the random symmetric $\pm 1$ Bernoulli ensemble.
artifact.status_search_result: A clean closed-form description of the finite-$n$ joint eigenvalue distribution of symmetric $\pm 1$ Bernoulli matrices does not appear in the literature. Available results (e.g., Guionnet's survey on Bernoulli random matrices, large-deviation/concentration results, and Wigner-type universality) describe asymptotic or qualitative behavior, not the exact finite-dimensional spectral law. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Bernoulli Random Matrices (Guionnet)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Bernoulli random matrices, focusing on asymptotic spectral and eigenvector properties, adjacency matrices of Erdős–Rényi graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys treat Bernoulli matrices through asymptotic/universality lenses, not exact finite-n spectral laws.

status_evidence.title: On the concentration of eigenvalues of random symmetric matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Large deviation bounds for eigenvalues of symmetric matrices with Bernoulli entries.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results on finite-n provide concentration/large deviation bounds rather than exact distributions.
